title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 28
description: Ten questions on Exodus 28: the holy garments for Aaron: the ephod, the breastplate, the robe and the gold plate.

questions.text: Which of these is named as one of Aaron's sons?
questions.explanation: Aaron's sons are named as Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

questions.text: Who were to make Aaron's garments?
questions.explanation: Moses was to speak to all who were wise-hearted, whom God had filled with the spirit of wisdom, to make Aaron's garments.

answers.text: Only men of the tribe of Levi

questions.text: In what order were the names engraved on the two onyx stones?
questions.explanation: Six names were on one stone and six on the other, in the order of their birth.

answers.text: By the size of each tribe
In the order of their birth

questions.text: Where were the two engraved onyx stones to be put?
questions.explanation: The two stones were put on the shoulder straps of the ephod, so Aaron would bear the names on his two shoulders as a memorial.

answers.text: On the shoulder straps of the ephod
On the front of the turban
On the hem of the blue robe

questions.text: Which stone was in the first row of the breastplate?
questions.explanation: The first row was a ruby, a topaz and a beryl.

questions.text: What was to be put in the breastplate of judgment?
questions.explanation: Moses was to put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastplate of judgment, to be on Aaron's heart.

questions.text: What color was the robe of the ephod?
questions.explanation: The robe of the ephod was to be made all of blue.

questions.text: Why was the sound of the golden bells to be heard when Aaron went into the holy place?
questions.explanation: The sound was to be heard when he went in and came out, so that he would not die.

answers.text: So that he would not die
To call the people to prayer
To mark the start of the feast

questions.text: What was engraved on the plate of pure gold?
questions.explanation: The plate of pure gold was engraved, like a signet, with "HOLY TO YAHWEH."

questions.text: How far were the linen pants to reach?
questions.explanation: The linen pants were to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs.

answers.text: From the knees to the ankles
From the shoulders to the waist
From the waist to the thighs
From the waist to the ankles
